title: Complex non-sterile compounding: statutory definition and licence requirement
subtopic: Complex non-sterile compounding definition and licence
rule_summary: As used in M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D and in ss. 36E to 42D, inclusive, unless the context clearly requires otherwise, s. 39D(a) defines complex non-sterile compounding as engaging in the compounding of a complex non-sterile drug preparation, and a complex non-sterile drug preparation as a compounded drug preparation which requires special training, a special environment or special facilities or equipment or the use of compounding techniques and procedures that may present an elevated risk to the compounder or the patient, as defined by the board through regulation, provided that the regulations promulgated by the board which are applicable to the definition shall be consistent with the category of complex non-sterile compounding described in chapter 795 of the USP. Under s. 39F(b), no pharmacy shall engage in complex non-sterile compounding nor shall a pharmacy prescribe, ship, mail, sell, transfer or dispense complex non-sterile drug preparations in the commonwealth unless the pharmacy has obtained a license from the board pursuant to section 39H or 39J.
exam_relevance: Tests that complex non-sterile compounding is a category defined in M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D that a pharmacy may undertake only under a licence from the Board.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws c. 112
authority.section: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(a), definitions of complex non-sterile compounding and complex non-sterile drug preparation

common_confusions: The definition turns on what the preparation requires, or on compounding techniques and procedures that may present an elevated risk to the compounder or the patient, as defined by the board through regulation.
Engaging in complex non-sterile compounding, or dispensing complex non-sterile drug preparations in the commonwealth, requires a license from the board pursuant to s. 39H or s. 39J.
